discovered.name: Analog bag / 'analog era' screen-free movement, and screen-free holiday gifting
discovered.whyConsidered: Several independent sources (Axios 2025, YPulse and Fortune April 2026, Fast Company, Eventbrite data, Michaels class) plus the PwC Holiday Outlook 2026 finding that 78% of Gen Z are prioritizing screen-free gifts. The trend lines up directly with holiday buying.

discovered.name: The Great Lock-In 2026 (aliases: Winter Arc, last-90-days challenge, 'lock in 2026')
discovered.whyConsidered: A named Sept 1 to Dec 31 self-improvement challenge, back for its second year (TheGrio 2026-09-01; BuzzFeed says it is 'taking over TikTok again'). It also carries into New Year 2027 'lock-in/rebrand' framing.

discovered.name: Gen Z / millennial Bible-reading revival ('quiet revival')
discovered.whyConsidered: Barna/Gloo measured Gen Z weekly Bible reading rising from 30% (2024) to 49% (2025). Record Bible sales are reported in the US and UK. New beginner guides launched in 2026. New Year reading plans are a natural seasonal hook.

discovered.name: Potential-maxxing / 'maxxing' trends
discovered.whyConsidered: Search summaries named potential-maxxing as a September 2026 trend, and Meltwater reported that use of 'maxxing' terms grew sharply in 2026.
discovered.rejectReason: The 'maxxing' umbrella covers unrelated behaviors, some of them drawing criticism and outrage (pheromone-maxxing). CNBC (2026-07-11) and Ohio State experts warn about health harms, so products would drift toward health claims. Only the 'log your progress with numbers' idea is kept, as a design feature in the Lock-In tracker.

discovered.name: Appstinence / dumbphone movement
discovered.whyConsidered: Plugged In, Movieguide and AOL describe Gen Z 'appstinence' and dumbphones. The search summary credited the term to founder Gabriela Nguyen.
discovered.rejectReason: This is the same underlying movement as the analog candidate, so it is merged there. The products it drives are mostly devices and apps (Light Phone, Brick). The term is tied to a named founder and organizations (Reconnect Movement), which raises attribution and rights concerns.

discovered.name: Gen Z New Year 'rebrand' instead of resolutions
discovered.whyConsidered: Trill Mag says Gen Z plans New Year 'rebrands' and 'lock-ins' months ahead using vision boards.
discovered.rejectReason: Thin evidence: essentially one publication, with no independent spread found. Merged into the Lock-In candidate's 2027 planner product.

discovered.name: Resolution / vision-board bingo card 2027
discovered.whyConsidered: A gamified goal-setting method (TikTok creator Erin Jones) that comes back every New Year, with 2027 versions already listed.
discovered.rejectReason: Saturated with free printables: Lovely Planner offers 13 free 2027 bingo cards, Parade has 7 printable 2027 cards, and Etsy already has 2027 bingo templates. The method dates from 2023-24, so nothing about it is new for 2027.

discovered.rejectReason: Established, with many free guides and kits. The evidence describes January 2026, not a new 2027 angle. It could appear as a single page inside a 2027 planner.

discovered.rejectReason: A recurring January ritual with heavy existing supply: an Etsy 'No Buy Challenge' market page and annual tracker listings. The supply gap is low. Better used as a bonus tracker page inside the Lock In 2027 planner than as a standalone launch.

discovered.rejectReason: It is already underway and lasts only one month. 'Go Sober for October' is a charity campaign name (Macmillan, UK). Products would sit close to health claims. There is no new 2026 twist.

candidates.name: Analog bag & screen-free holiday gifting
candidates.summary: Young adults are filling a tote with screen-free activities (books, puzzles, crafts, a notebook) to avoid doomscrolling, and that preference is now shaping 2026 holiday gift lists.
candidates.what: An 'analog bag' is a tote packed with non-digital activities (crosswords, sketchbook, crochet, a camera, a book) carried so people reach for it instead of their phone. It is the most visible object of a broader 2026 'analog' movement that also includes paper planners, phone-free events and dumbphones. For holiday 2026, PwC reports that most Gen Z shoppers are prioritizing screen-free gifts.

origin.text: Traced in press to TikTok creators in 2025. Axios covered the analog bag as a screen-free wellness trend in October 2025, and the search summary named micro-influencers including Siece Campbell. PureWow called it the hottest holiday gift of 2025.

adopters.text: Mainly Gen Z and young millennial women, according to YPulse and Fast Company, who want to cut doomscrolling and reclaim attention. It has since spread to parents gifting teens and tweens (PureWow) and to faith and lifestyle bloggers (Karen Ehman). PwC's 2026 holiday survey finds 78% of Gen Z prioritizing screen-free gifts, against 64% of all consumers.

spread.text: Coverage has spread well beyond TikTok: trend trackers (YPulse, April 2026), business press (Fortune April and September 2026, Fast Company), fashion and general-interest titles (Marie Claire, Reader's Digest), a major craft retailer running a 'What's in your analog bag' class (Michaels), Eventbrite's own event data, and PwC's holiday survey. These are independent outlets, not reposts of one article.

trajectory.text: It has moved from a 2025 TikTok niche to mainstream coverage and survey-tracked behavior in 2026. Eventbrite reports phone-free events up 567% globally from 2024 to 2025. Holiday 2026 is the second gifting season for the trend, and PwC's September survey shows it shaping gift intent. Inference: interest is still rising heading into the holidays, but saturation (free printables, mass-retail kits) is the main risk.

productDemand.text: There is gift-purchase intent for the screen-free categories themselves: PwC lists puzzles, art supplies, board games and books, and 81% of Gen Z prioritize in-person holiday activities. Press frames the analog bag explicitly as a gift (PureWow 2025; Karen Ehman suggests stocking stuffers). There is no direct evidence that people buy printable analog-bag content as opposed to physical items. PwC also projects Gen Z gift spending down 9%, which favors low-price items.

competition.text: An Etsy market page for 'analog bag' exists, and search results show mostly kids' screen-free activity and coloring packs at about $0.99-$6.99. analogbag.net gives away free coloring pages and plans puzzles and journal templates. Generic journal-prompt printables are saturated and cheap. Mass retailers sell the physical fillers. No adult-focused, giftable printable 'refill pack' or phone-free gathering kit was seen in results, but listing counts could not be checked because Etsy was blocked.

gap.text: Missing: (1) an adult or teen-focused, gift-ready printable 'analog bag refill' with original puzzles and prompts, packaged to print and tuck into a tote or stocking at the last minute; (2) a 'phone-free table' kit for Friendsgiving and holiday dinners, tying the 81% in-person / 63% shared-meal preference to the growth in phone-free events; (3) a tote whose design is the analog bag itself, as an illustrated contents map with no brand marks. Existing printables skew toward kids and coloring.

window.estimate: Now through Dec 24, 2026 for digital; POD orders by about Dec 8-10 for Christmas delivery; then January 2027 digital-detox season
window.reasoning: PwC's gift intent applies to this holiday season. Digital delivers instantly, so it fits last-minute buyers (Basis reports 83% decide within days of discovering a gift; evidence a22). New listings need weeks to surface, so they should go up in October. The movement has run from 2025 through 2026 across independent outlets, so it will probably outlast the product cycle.
invalidators: Free printable sites (e.g. analogbag.net) fill the adult segment
Etsy search does not surface new listings before mid-December
Backlash framing analog as aesthetic overconsumption
Physical kits from big retailers crowd out digital gift alternatives
window.seasonality: Peak gifting from mid-November to Dec 24; secondary peak in January (detox and New Year habits).

rights.note: 'Analog bag' reads as a generic community term, but trademark filings were not checked (search budget ran out). Avoid brand names and trade dress: Polaroid, Instax/Fujifilm, Brick, Light Phone, The Offline Club, NYT Crossword/Wordle. Write all puzzles from scratch. Do not use creators' names or likenesses.

timing.rationale: PwC (September 2026) shows screen-free gift intent for this holiday season. There are 10-11 weeks of selling time for digital.

buyerIntent.rationale: Gift intent for screen-free categories is reported. Intent for printable (digital) versions specifically is unproven.

supplyGap.rationale: An Etsy market exists, free printables are available, and generic prompts are saturated. The gap is narrow: adult and gift positioning, phone-free gathering kits.

productFit.rationale: Printables and POD totes are easy for a solo AI-assisted creator. Original puzzles take care to get right.

durability.rationale: Sustained from 2025 through 2026 across many independent sources and Eventbrite data. It is a movement, not a single meme.

economics.rationale: Digital margins are high, but price points are low ($4-9). POD tote margins are thin after base cost and fees.

candidates.actionRationale: There is independent, multi-source evidence of a lasting movement, plus fresh survey evidence of screen-free gift intent for holiday 2026. Digital products can be built in 2-3 days and listed in October, leaving time for discovery. Test the gift-ready refill pack and the phone-free table kit first. Treat the tote as a secondary test with a hard POD cutoff in early December.

products.buyer: Gen Z/millennial women aged 18-34, and gift-givers (friends, parents of teens) looking for a screen-free gift or stocking stuffer
products.theme: 'Analog Bag Refill Pack': about 40 printable half-letter/A5 pages that fold into pocket booklets. Contents: original crosswords, word searches and logic grids; 30 sketch prompts; 52 journal prompts; an 'offline bingo' card; a cut-and-fold mini-zine; and a printable gift tag reading 'Your analog bag awaits'.
products.whyBuy: Puzzles and art activities match the categories PwC says Gen Z wants as screen-free gifts. As a digital download it works as an instant last-minute gift or a tote/stocking filler.
products.differentiation: Designed for adults and teens, unlike the kids' activity packs and free coloring pages. Packaged as a gift (tag, booklet fold). All puzzles original. Coordinated aesthetic with the tote.
products.validationTest: List on Etsy and Gumroad by Oct 10. Post 10 Pinterest pins (keywords 'analog bag ideas', 'screen-free gift') and 3 short 'pack my analog bag' videos. Run $1-2/day Etsy ads for 14 days.
products.continueIf: At least one sale, or a clearly rising favorites-to-views ratio, within 14 days of ads starting; pins getting saves.
products.pivotIf: Views and favorites but no sales: reposition as a family/teen 'phone-free holiday' pack, or bundle it with the table kit.
products.stopIf: Fewer than about 100 listing views after 21 days of ads, or no sales by Nov 20.
products.rightsNote: Write every puzzle and prompt from scratch. Do not imitate NYT/Wordle branding. Use the word 'analog' generically.

products.theme: 'Phone-Free Table Kit': a phone-basket sign ('Phones rest here tonight'), 60 conversation cards, 4 pen-and-paper party games, and place cards. Two editions: Friendsgiving (week of Nov 26) and Christmas/New Year's Eve.
products.whyBuy: 81% of Gen Z prioritize in-person holiday activities and 63% say a shared meal matters more than a present (PwC via Fortune). Phone-free events are surging (Eventbrite). Hosts want an easy, instantly downloadable way to make a dinner feel offline.
products.differentiation: Uses phone-free as the hook, unlike generic Friendsgiving trivia and invitations. Works for several holidays from one design system.
products.validationTest: Publish the Friendsgiving edition by Oct 20 with pins targeting 'Friendsgiving games' and 'phone-free party'. Track listing views and saves weekly.
products.continueIf: Any sales or steady favorite growth by Nov 15. If so, launch the Christmas/NYE edition by Nov 25.
products.pivotIf: Friendsgiving edition gets views but no sales: drop it and put effort into the NYE 'phone-free countdown' edition.
products.stopIf: Under 50 views by Nov 10 despite pins and ads.
products.rightsNote: Original game rules and text. Do not use trademarked game names (Pictionary, Scattergories, etc.).

products.buyer: Analog-curious Gen Z/millennials, and people buying a tote to build an analog bag as a gift
products.theme: An illustrated 'contents map' tote: line drawings of a paperback, unbranded film camera, crochet hook and yarn, pocket crossword and pencil, with a small original phrase (e.g. 'Gone analog').
products.whyBuy: The bag is the object at the center of the trend, so the tote doubles as both gift and container. Press frames analog bags as a holiday gift.
products.differentiation: Illustration-led rather than slogan-only. Pairs with the refill pack as a 'gift set' listing.
products.validationTest: List from mockups by Oct 15 and order one sample to check print quality. Promote the gift-set pairing with the refill pack.
products.pivotIf: Totes get views but no sales: offer the illustration as a sticker sheet or printable art instead.
products.stopIf: No sales by Dec 5 (practical POD cutoff for Christmas delivery).
products.rightsNote: Draw a generic camera, not a recognizable Polaroid/Instax shape. Run a trademark search on any phrase before use (not done here).

candidates.name: The Great Lock-In 2026 (end-of-year self-improvement sprint)
candidates.summary: A TikTok-born challenge where people use September 1 to December 31 to build habits and work on goals, instead of waiting for New Year's resolutions.
candidates.what: Participants pick a small set of personal goals (fitness, money, reading, sleep, organization, and in 2026 more mindfulness) and 'lock in' on them for the last four months of the year. There are no official rules. It started on TikTok in August 2025 and returned for 2026. It overlaps with the older 'Winter Arc' (Oct 1 to Dec 31) and 'last 90 days' challenges, and feeds the 'lock-in/rebrand instead of resolutions' framing for the New Year.

origin.text: Became widely known on TikTok in late August and early September 2025. Fortune covered it on 2025-09-11 as a Gen Z rejection of the 'soft life'. SEO explainers say it started on TikTok in August 2025 and returns every September. 'Lock in' is described as UK-origin slang for hyper-focusing.

adopters.text: Gen Z and young millennials on TikTok, with coverage of adoption in Black online communities (The Root, TheGrio). Fitness and wellness brands (Gymshark, Johnson Fitness UK) and productivity apps (Motion, HabitHuddle) publish content about it. People want structure and a fresh start without waiting for January.

spread.text: In 2025: Fortune, CTV/CP24, CBC (critical), Newsweek (per explainers), a Know Your Meme entry. In 2026: TheGrio (2026-09-01, syndicated by Yahoo), BuzzFeed ('taking over TikTok again'), a Yahoo homebuying angle, and many SEO explainer pages. Brands and apps produce their own content. Attention is spreading independently, but much of the 2026 coverage restates the explainer.

trajectory.text: This is the second annual cycle, with mainstream coverage in 2026 describing a broader, more holistic version. Within the year, attention likely peaks around Sept 1 (inference from timing), and we are already 34 days in. The sibling alias 'Winter Arc' shows how fast these names churn: spiketoday reports its 2025 Google Trends peak was about a quarter of the 2024 peak. Inference: the end-of-year sprint ritual is durable, but any single name may fade within 1-2 years.

productDemand.text: Most signals are participation and curiosity content (videos documenting rules and routines) rather than purchase intent. Paid products exist for the sibling Winter Arc trend (Gumroad and Payhip journals and trackers), and Etsy sells many generic habit trackers at $1-6, which shows people buy trackers in general. No sales data for lock-in-branded products was found. Trill Mag reports Gen Z replacing resolutions with 'rebrands' and 'lock-ins' planned months ahead, which supports a New Year 2027 planner angle.

competition.text: Generic printable habit trackers are saturated on Etsy. Free apps (Motion, HabitHuddle) publish Winter Arc and Lock-In guides. Winter Arc journals are sold on Gumroad. A search for lock-in-specific Etsy trackers returned only generic trackers, which suggests few trend-named listings, but Etsy could not be checked directly.

gap.text: A dated 'final 12 weeks of 2026' Lock-In tracker that includes a progress log for proving results with numbers (borrowing the 2026 'potential-maxxing' habit of quantifying growth), and especially a 'Lock In 2027' quarterly sprint planner that carries the lock-in identity into January for resolution skeptics. Existing products are either generic trackers or tied to the fading 'Winter Arc' name.

window.estimate: Sprint tracker: now to mid-November at best. 'Lock In 2027' planner: list by Dec 1, sell Dec 15 to Jan 31
window.reasoning: The 2026 lock-in started Sept 1 and is already a month old. A new listing needs weeks to surface, so a Sept-Dec tracker mostly misses the window. New Year planning is the stronger window, and the 'lock-in instead of resolutions' framing is documented.
invalidators: The 'Great Lock-In' name fades the way 'Winter Arc' did
TikTok moves to a new name for the January reset
Backlash about burnout and 'grind culture' (CBC critique) reduces appeal
Free app templates meet the need
window.seasonality: Two peaks a year: early September (lock-in start) and late December to early January (resolution season). Winter Arc peaks around Oct 1.

rights.note: 'Great Lock-In', 'lock in' and 'winter arc' read as community slang, but trademark filings were not checked (search budget ran out). Avoid brand names (Gymshark), creator names and likenesses, and any health or fitness outcome claims.

supplyGap.rationale: Few trend-named products were seen (unverified, Etsy blocked), but generic trackers and free apps substitute easily.

productFit.rationale: A dated tracker or planner is a quick, low-risk printable.

durability.rationale: The ritual recurs every year, but names churn: Winter Arc's 2025 peak was about a quarter of 2024's, per spiketoday.

economics.rationale: Digital at $3-9 with near-zero cost, and an optional KDP paperback. Prices are low.

candidates.actionRationale: The trend is real and covered by mainstream press in 2026, but purchase intent is unproven and the 2026 sprint window is closing. A one-day '12 final weeks' tracker is a cheap way to test the name now. The main bet is a 'Lock In 2027' planner listed by Dec 1 for the resolution season.

candidates.name: Gen Z & millennial Bible-reading revival
candidates.summary: Surveys and sales data report sharply more young US and UK adults reading and buying Bibles, with young men prominent. That creates new readers who need beginner-friendly structure, especially at New Year.
candidates.what: Barna and Gloo's State of the Church research (released November 2025) reports US weekly Bible reading rebounding to 42% of adults, with Gen Z rising from 30% to 49% and young men leading. Physical Bible sales are reported at a 21-year US high in 2025 and record UK levels. Publishers have launched beginner guides for 'a new generation of readers'. This describes reported engagement data, not any particular teaching.

origin.text: UK reports of a 'quiet revival' and rising Bible sales date from 2024-2025. US data came from Barna/Gloo's State of the Church release in November 2025, and coverage continued into 2026 (Shoutout UK April 2026; a beginner guide launched for Easter 2026).

adopters.text: Gen Z and millennials, especially young men, according to Barna. Pastors report higher Gen Z engagement: 45% versus 12% reporting lower (Crosswalk). Press reports first-time Bible buyers, and Gen Z reportedly prefers 'aesthetic' editions and journaling Bibles. Motivations described in press include searching for meaning; this is a reported framing, not an inference about individuals.

spread.text: Reported by research firms (Barna/Gloo), denominational and Christian press (Baptist Press, Christian Post, Crosswalk, Christian Institute), UK youth media (Shoutout UK), retailers (Eden) and publishers (ilubra press release). Mainstream secular coverage was not checked in depth (search budget). Much of the US coverage traces back to one Barna/Gloo dataset, so it counts as one primary signal with many reports.

trajectory.text: Measured growth from a 2024 low (Barna) and sales reported rising since 2019 (UK +106% per Christian Institute), with 2026 product launches responding to new readers. Inference: early growth within the youth segment of a large, established religious-publishing niche. Christian Post notes fewer respondents believe the Bible is fully accurate, so the picture is mixed rather than uniformly 'revival'.

productDemand.text: There is direct purchase evidence for Bibles themselves (record sales reported). Publishers launched beginner reference guides in 2026, which shows a perceived need for orientation tools. Etsy sells low-priced Bible reading trackers (e.g. a chronological plan at $1.87 from a Star Seller). Demand for printable reading plans for new young readers specifically is plausible but not measured. Free plans from churches and apps are a strong substitute.

competition.text: High. Reading-plan printables and trackers are abundant and cheap on Etsy, free plans are widespread from churches and Bible apps, and journaling Bibles and devotionals are an established publishing category. Beginner orientation guides exist (ilubra). Less visible in results: plans explicitly designed for first-time young-adult readers, and styles aimed at the young-men segment Barna highlights.

gap.text: A 2027 'first-time reader' plan: references only, two styles (minimal for young men, soft aesthetic), plus factual orientation pages (how the Bible is organized: testaments, books, genres) and a simple tracker. Also a neutral reading-notes journal. Neither should present new teachings or promise outcomes. The opening is in beginner positioning and design rather than content novelty.

window.estimate: List by about Dec 1, 2026 and sell through mid-January 2027 (New Year reading-plan season). The underlying trend looks multi-year.
window.reasoning: Year-long reading plans conventionally start January 1 (inference; no search evidence gathered on seasonal spikes). The revival data covers multiple years (sales up since 2019 in the UK; US rebound 2024 to 2025), so the trend should outlast the launch window.
invalidators: 2026 State of the Church or other surveys show the rebound reversing or not replicating
Free app and church plans fully meet the need
Community reaction to commercial products seen as inauthentic
Translation-copyright problems if scripture text is included
window.seasonality: Peak late December to mid-January for year-long plans. Secondary peaks around Lent/Easter and back-to-school.

rights.note: Modern translations (NIV, ESV, NLT, CSB, etc.) are copyrighted and have quotation permissions. Use references only, or quote public-domain text (KJV, World English Bible). Do not use ministry or app brand names (YouVersion, She Reads Truth, BibleProject) or the names of published reading plans unless they are verified public domain. Have content checked for accuracy and denominational neutrality. Make no claims about spiritual or mental-health outcomes.

timing.rationale: Ten weeks to prepare for the New Year reading-plan season; the trend is in growth.

buyerIntent.rationale: Bible purchases are reported at record levels. Intent for printable plans is unmeasured and free substitutes are common.

supplyGap.rationale: Crowded category. The opening is narrow positioning: first-time young adults, design for young men.

productFit.rationale: Printables and KDP journals are easy to make, but accuracy and sensitivity review add effort.

durability.rationale: Multi-year data (UK sales since 2019; US rebound 2024 to 2025) and continuing 2026 coverage.

economics.rationale: Digital $4-9 and KDP journals; prices are pushed down by $2 trackers and free plans.

candidates.actionRationale: Durable, measured growth among exactly the young adults who buy printables. But competition is high and the seasonal window opens in late December, so build carefully, with accuracy review and references only, and list by about Dec 1 rather than rushing a test now.

products.buyer: Adults aged 18-35 who are new to reading the Bible, including first-time Bible buyers; separate design for the young-men segment
products.theme: '2027 First-Time Reader Plan': a references-only, one-year reading schedule based on a standard, verifiable structure (e.g. the whole Bible in canonical or chronological order, or the New Testament in a year), plus orientation pages (how the Bible is organized: testaments, book list, genres), a check-off tracker and a notes page. Offered in two visual styles.
products.whyBuy: Weekly Bible reading among Gen Z is reported up from 30% to 49%, and new readers want structure. Publishers launched beginner guides in 2026. January 1 is the natural start date.
products.differentiation: Built for beginners, with factual orientation pages. A minimal style for young men, unlike the mostly floral tracker designs. No copyrighted text.
products.validationTest: List both styles by Nov 20 and pin weekly. Watch which style earns more favorites and clicks by Dec 20.
products.continueIf: Sales, or favorites growing week over week, during Dec 15 to Jan 10.
products.pivotIf: Only one style moves: drop the other and add a matching journal or Bible-tab printable in the winning style.
products.rightsNote: References only. No translation text. Do not copy proprietary reading plans. Get an accuracy review.

products.buyer: The same new readers who prefer writing by hand
products.theme: An undated 365-entry reading-notes journal with neutral fields (date, passage reference, what stood out, questions, notes or prayer) and orientation pages at the front, in the two matching styles.
products.whyBuy: Journaling Bibles and handwritten notes are reported as Gen Z preferences, and this fits the analog/paper trend.
products.differentiation: Matches the plan's design and beginner orientation, and pairs with it as a bundle.
products.validationTest: Publish to KDP by Dec 1 (allowing for review time) and sell the digital interior on Etsy.
products.continueIf: Any organic KDP sales in the first three weeks of January.
products.pivotIf: KDP stalls but digital sells: keep digital only.
products.stopIf: No sales in either channel by Jan 31, 2027.
products.rightsNote: Do not present common journaling methods as new teachings. No scripture text unless public domain.

unresolved: Do Barna's 2025 figures hold in 2026 data, and do other surveys (e.g. Pew, Gallup) agree? Not checked because the search budget ran out.
